title: Wipro Beats Second-Quarter Revenue Estimates as Europe Spending Revives
excerpt: Revenue rose 9.1% to $2.60 billion, but profit missed estimates and deal wins fell to $2.6 billion from $4.7 billion a year earlier.
body:
• Wipro's second-quarter consolidated revenue rose 9.1% to 247.53 billion rupees ($2.60 billion), slightly above the LSEG analyst estimate of 246.27 billion rupees.
  • Net profit was 32.01 billion rupees, below the 33.69 billion rupees analysts had expected, even as revenue beat.
  • Total deal wins fell to $2.6 billion from $4.7 billion a year earlier, despite new pacts with ABB, CrowdStrike and Aramco.
  • Reader utility: Wipro guided third-quarter revenue to $2.57-$2.63 billion, implying a 1.5% fall to 0.5% growth — the range investors will test against peers TCS and HCLTech.

Wipro, India's fourth-largest information technology services company, reported second-quarter revenue slightly above expectations on Thursday, helped by reviving spending among European clients and new revenue linked to artificial intelligence work.

Consolidated revenue for the July-September quarter rose 9.1 percent to 247.53 billion rupees, or $2.60 billion, according to Reuters reporting on the results, just ahead of the 246.27 billion rupees average estimate compiled by LSEG. Net profit, at 32.01 billion rupees, came in below the 33.69 billion rupees analysts had forecast.

Europe and AI did the heavy lifting

Revenue from Europe, which accounts for more than a fourth of Wipro's business, rose 5.1 percent year over year after stripping out currency movements. The company pointed to partnerships signed during the year with Anthropic and Google as helping it build AI-related revenue and savings.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4H9S97A7uIw

The pattern matches the wider Indian IT earnings season. Larger rivals Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech reported revenue broadly in line with estimates, but their shares rose as investors rewarded evidence of AI revenue. Wipro's Mumbai-listed shares had closed 1.4 percent higher ahead of the results, with the Nifty IT index up 1.7 percent.

The Hindu BusinessLine's live results coverage separately noted a 9.5 percent rise in standalone profit after tax to 2,862.7 crore rupees, against 2,614.2 crore rupees a year earlier — a different, standalone measure from the consolidated net profit reported by Reuters.

Deal bookings are the weak spot

The clear soft patch was order intake. Total deal wins fell to $2.6 billion from $4.7 billion a year earlier. Wipro did sign agreements during the quarter with industrial group ABB, cybersecurity company CrowdStrike and oil major Aramco, but the headline total suggests large-deal momentum slowed compared with a strong comparison period.

For investors, that gap matters more than the small revenue beat. IT services revenue is booked over time, so a thinner deal pipeline today can mean slower growth several quarters out, unless smaller and AI-led engagements convert faster than traditional large deals.

Guidance for the December quarter

Wipro forecast third-quarter revenue of $2.57 billion to $2.63 billion. That translates to a decline of 1.5 percent to growth of 0.5 percent, a range the company set against brokerage expectations that had centred on a 2 percent decline to flat growth. In other words, guidance was not strong in absolute terms, but it was marginally better than the cautious range many analysts had pencilled in.

What it means

The quarter leaves Wipro in a familiar position: operations steady, Europe improving, AI partnerships building, but profit and deal bookings short of the strongest hopes. The stock's next move will depend less on the 9.1 percent revenue rise already reported and more on whether management can show that AI work is turning into larger, repeatable contracts.

Investors will also compare Wipro's guidance with demand commentary from TCS and HCLTech, and watch client budgets in Europe and North America heading into the new calendar year, when technology spending plans are typically reset. A recovery in large-deal signings would do more to change the narrative than another small quarterly beat.
